Variants.Content: Entry Succession in Westeros generally favors the legitimate eldest son, but local custom, family paperwork, royal edicts, and actual power can make exceptions to the rule. Dorne admits that the eldest daughter is given priority. Some families value the nearest blood relatives or local traditions; illegitimate children will not succeed by default The role of inheritance law is not to automatically select people who cannot be challenged, but to provide language for disputes that each party can invoke. Legitimacy, consanguinity, wills, vassal recognition, and force may conflict with each other.

Entry Succession Succession and Legitimization: Succession in Westeros generally favors the legitimate eldest son, but local custom, family paperwork, royal edicts, and actual power can make exceptions to the rule. Dorne admits that the eldest daughter is given priority. Some families value the nearest blood relatives or local traditions; illegitimate children will not succeed by default. They start by asking who is obligated, who is protected, and who will seek justice after a breach of contract.
